metadata.notes: A THIRD, genuinely different COMBINE-shaped action in this vocabulary (after combine.json/combine_potato_onion.json — combine_con_cebolla.json is a fourth, structurally distinct COMBINE-shaped step) — target: flour (isDoughBase, a NEW capability, not reusing potato.json's/potato_onion_mixture.json's isCombinableBase, on purpose: flour combining into dough is a genuinely different real pairing, and this repo's own capabilityAmbiguityNote on potato_onion_mixture.json already names the real risk of two COMBINE-shaped actions sharing one capability by accident — a dedicated flag avoids adding a THIRD action to that same ambiguity). Secondary: water (isDoughLiquid, also new — see water.json's own isDoughLiquidNote for why this isn't isBoilingMedium/isDissolvingMedium/isPourable reused). requiredTools: ['bowl'], same reasoning as the original combine.json (a real mixing vessel, not the tool-free combine_potato_onion.json case — raw sliced potato+onion are just placed together in a pan, but flour+water genuinely need to be mixed in a bowl first).
metadata.hydrationNote: This action does NOT take a water-quantity/hydration-percentage parameter — the real ~65% baker's-percentage figure dough.json's own composition citation uses is a MODELING assumption for that entity's composition data, not something this step lets a caller vary per-call. A real, honest simplification: this vocabulary's QuantitySchema (ingredient.ts) already lets a recipe author specify precise gram amounts for flour-1/water-1 in initialInventory, so the REAL hydration ratio of any given recipe is still expressible — this action just doesn't compute or validate it.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): a single one-off assembly of two instances into one — same reasoning as combine.json's identical note; both discriminators agree.

verification.description: Flour and water are combined into one cohesive, if rough and uneven ('shaggy'), mass — no dry, unincorporated flour remains
